language.name: The language's own name, as its speakers write it: Français, Deutsch, 日本語.
desktop.comment: The application's description in Linux menus. A test lists the line to add to apps/desktop/src-tauri/reroute.desktop and crates/platform/src/register/linux.rs.
settings.title: Title bar of the settings window.
picker.remember: Checkbox under the browsers. {host} is the link's host name, shown in bold.
picker.hint: The picker's keys, in its footer: digits pick a browser, arrows move, Enter opens, Esc cancels. Use the names printed on keyboards in your language. Very little room.
picker.update.current: Beside a small button in the picker's footer; little room. {version} is a version number such as 0.2.0.
picker.update.available: Beside a small button in the picker's footer; little room. {version} is a version number such as 0.2.0.
picker.settings.title: Tooltip of the ⚙ button. The comma is the key that opens the settings: keep it.
picker.tile.withLaunches: Read by screen readers for a browser that has launch options (profiles, private windows).
picker.menu.default: First entry of a browser's launch menu: the browser started with no special option.
picker.refused: {reason} is one of the rust.url.* messages, already translated.
settings.loadError: Keep the file names config.toml and config.toml.broken as they are. {reason} is one of the rust.* messages, already translated.
settings.savedBroken: Keep the file name config.toml.broken as it is.
settings.unexpected.console: Fills {detail} of settings.unexpected when the error has no message.
browsers.detected: {count} is a number of browsers added to the list.
browsers.hidden: A tag beside a browser's name in the list: the browser does not appear in the picker.
browsers.args: {url} is the literal marker %URL%, shown as code.
browsers.launches: Heading. A launch option is another way to start a browser, such as a profile.
browsers.launch.namePlaceholder: Example name shown in an empty field.
rules.problem: One line per faulty pattern. {pattern} is the pattern as typed, {problem} one of the rules.problem.* texts.
rules.test.match: {browser} is shown in bold, {pattern} as code, {ruleset} is the ruleset's name.
rules.test.matchLaunch: {browser} is shown in bold, {launch} is a launch option's name, {pattern} as code, {ruleset} is the ruleset's name.
general.hurl: Hurl is the name of another program: do not translate it.
general.hurl.help: {file} is the file name UserSettings.json, shown as code.
general.hurl.done: {browsers} is general.hurl.browsers and {rulesets} general.hurl.rulesets, already counted.
about.privacy: {http} and {https} are the words http and https, shown as code.
rust.config.pattern: {problem} is one of the rust.pattern.* messages, already translated.
rust.file: {path} is a file's path; {detail} is what the system said, in English.
rust.hurl.bad_rule: {rule} is a rule as Hurl writes it, such as d$example.com; {problem} is one of the rust.pattern.* messages.
rust.launch.spawn: {program} is a path; {detail} is what the system said, in English.
rust.pick.remember: {host} is a host name; {problem} is one of the rust.pattern.* messages.
rust.register.confirm_windows: Use the name Windows gives its Settings app in your language.
rust.release.status: {status} is an HTTP status code, such as 500.
rust.url.scheme_not_allowed: {scheme} is what a link starts with, before the colon: javascript, ftp, file…
